export_raw_verification.scope:
Raw export of data that cannot be recovered as a verified file (damaged media).

A synthetic NTFS volume is acquired, one 512-byte block of a fragmented file is
marked permanently unreadable in the read map, and normal recovery must still
refuse to invent bytes. export-raw must then write exactly the readable bytes
with the unreadable range zero-filled, list that range in a JSON map, mark the
output unverified, never overwrite, and refuse a destination on the source.
Expected bytes are computed here from the fixture truth, independently of Rust.

damaged_fat_verification.scope:
Damaged USB/SD FAT32 media: one FAT mirror overwritten, cut or unreadable.

Each case damages only one of the two FAT copies of a synthetic volume. Recovery
must use the single copy that gives a loop-free chain (of the recorded length for
files), recover every expected file byte-exact and say so in the scan warnings.
When both copies give different valid chains the volume must still be refused,
because choosing one would be a guess. An unreadable FAT sector in an acquired
image is handled the same way. Truth bytes come from the fixture generator.

damaged_fat_verification.scope:
Damaged USB/SD FAT32 media: one FAT mirror overwritten, cut or unreadable.

Each case damages only one of the two FAT copies of a synthetic volume. Recovery
must use the single copy that gives a loop-free chain (of the recorded length for
files), recover every expected file byte-exact and say so in the scan warnings.
When both copies give different valid chains the volume must still be refused,
because choosing one would be a guess. An unreadable FAT sector in an acquired
image is handled the same way. Truth bytes come from the fixture generator.

known_hashes_verification.scope:
Known SHA-256 comparison of real recovery records, with honest recorded-digest scope.

Content matches never certify an original name, remove uncertainty, or imply that

cp932_verification.scope:
Explicit CP932 FAT 8.3 names, raw provenance and durable settings.

Uses Python's independent CP932 codec and ordinary FAT12/16/32 fixtures. Deleted
leading bytes remain unknown; ambiguous DBCS boundaries are never picked silently.
